content: There is no evidence to suggest that avibactam has any adverse effects on embryofetal development. However, since animal reproduction studies do not always predict human responses, this medication should only be used during pregnancy if it is clearly necessary. Ceftazidime is excreted into human breast milk in low concentrations. It is currently unknown whether avibactam is excreted into human breast milk, although studies have shown that avibactam is excreted into the milk of rats. There is no available information regarding the effects of ceftazidime and avibactam on a breastfed child or on milk production. Ceftazidime/avibactam, commonly marketed under the brand name Avycaz, is a combination medication used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. Ceftazidime is a cephalosporin antibiotic that works by inhibiting bacterial growth. This medication is effective only against bacterial infections and will not treat viral infections such as the common cold or flu. This medication is administered intravenously, typically every 8 hours over a 2-hour infusion period, as directed by a healthcare provider. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on the patient’s medical condition and response to therapy. If used at home, patients should be thoroughly instructed by a healthcare professional on the preparation and administration of the medication. The solution should appear clear and light yellow; if particles or discoloration are observed, the solution should not be used. For optimal efficacy, this antibiotic should be administered at evenly spaced intervals. It is crucial to complete the full prescribed course of treatment, even if symptoms resolve after a few days, to prevent the development of antibiotic resistance. Common side effects of this medication include nausea, vomiting, constipation, and anxiety. It is important to note that this medication has been prescribed because the healthcare provider has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition known as Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea, which can occur during or even weeks to months after treatment. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare but possible. Before using this medication, patients should inform their healthcare provider if they are allergic to ceftazidime, avibactam, penicillins, beta-lactam antibiotics, other cephalosporins, or beta-lactamase inhibitors such as sulbactam. Additionally, patients should disclose any other allergies or medical conditions. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. Ceftazidime/avibactam may interfere with the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. While ceftazidime is known to pass into breast milk, it is unclear whether avibactam does. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of this medication or increase the risk of serious side effects. Patients should maintain a comprehensive list of all medications and supplements they are taking and share this information with their healthcare provider. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as Coombs’ tests or urine glucose tests, potentially leading to false results. In the event of an overdose, immediate medical attention is required. If the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, emergency services should be contacted. For non-emergency overdoses, a poison control center should be contacted immediately. This medication should only be used for the condition for which it was prescribed. Regular laboratory and medical tests, such as kidney function tests, should be conducted during treatment to monitor the patient’s response and detect any potential side effects. Patients should attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If a dose is missed, the patient should consult their healthcare provider or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Proper storage of this medication is essential, and patients should follow the storage instructions provided by their pharmacist or the product label. Medications should not be disposed of by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Expired or unused medication should be discarded properly. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Patients should always consult their healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and their specific health needs.
